title: Old King Cole
transcription:
Old King Cole
A progression song

Old King Cole was a merry old soul
and a merry old soul was he,
He called for his pipe
and he called for his bowl
and he called for his:

Privates three:
'Rooty-Tooty-Tooty-Toot'
say the Privates

ending chorus:
Merry Men are we,
and there's none so fair
as can compare, to the boys
from old Cherry.

Sergeants three:
'Heeeeyyyy-up' say the Sergeants
'Rooty-Tooty-Tooty-Tooty-Toot'
say the Privates

Captains three:
'We want leave for a year!' say the Captains
'Heeeeyyyy-up' say the Sergeants
'Rooty-Tooty-Tooty-Tooty-Toot'
say the Privates

Generals three:
'Where's my big white horse!' say the Generals
'We want leave for a year!' say the Captains
'Heeeeyyyy-up' say the Sergeants
'Rooty-Tooty-Tooty-Tooty-Toot'
say the Privates

Start each verse with Old King Cole... and
end with 'Merry Men are we...'
The crowd can be broken into smaller groups,
and each group assigned a 'Rooty' etc. pri-
vates, sergeants, etc) to repeat.
